negate.description: Negate makes this a negative permission

callback_url.description:
Deprecated: send redirect_uris instead. If both are sent, callback_url
must equal the first entry of redirect_uris.

redirect_uris.description:
RedirectURIs is the ordered list of URIs the app may redirect to. The
first entry is the primary. Required, unless the deprecated
callback_url is sent instead.

scope.description:
Scope is the space-separated list of scopes this app's tokens may be
granted. Leave empty, or omit, for unrestricted.

app_name.description:
AppName is any name for the app reporting usage. The server normalizes
it at ingestion, so a new app needs no server change. The UsageAppName
constants are the well-known names.

failure_hard_limit.description:
FailureHardLimit defines the maximum number of consecutive failed prebuild attempts allowed
before a preset is considered to be in a hard limit state. When a preset hits this limit,
no new prebuilds will be created until the limit is reset.
FailureHardLimit is disabled when set to zero.

reconciliation_backoff_interval.description:
ReconciliationBackoffInterval specifies the amount of time to increase the backoff interval
when errors occur during reconciliation.

reconciliation_backoff_lookback.description:
ReconciliationBackoffLookback determines the time window to look back when calculating
the number of failed prebuilds, which influences the backoff strategy.

reconciliation_interval.description: ReconciliationInterval defines how often the workspace prebuilds state should be reconciled.

id.description:
ID identifies this click, and doubles as the attribution token that a
later trial signup reports.

daemons.description: Daemons is the number of built-in terraform provisioners.

disable_module_cache.description:
DisableModuleCache disables the reuse of Terraform modules cached at
template import for every template in the deployment. Templates cannot
opt back in.

errors.description: Errors are problems that prevent the workspace proxy from being healthy

warnings.description:
Warnings do not prevent the workspace proxy from being healthy, but
should be addressed.

condition.description:
Condition is required for the condition mode and must be empty
otherwise.

expected_revision.description:
ExpectedRevision must equal the current revision of the stored rule,
or zero when no rule is stored or the stored rule has no readable
positive revision. A different revision fails with 409 Conflict.

callback_url.description:
Deprecated: send redirect_uris instead. If both are sent, callback_url
must equal the first entry of redirect_uris.

icon.description:
Icon replaces the app's stored icon. Omitting it clears the stored
icon rather than leaving it unchanged.

redirect_uris.description:
RedirectURIs is the ordered list of URIs the app may redirect to. The
first entry is the primary. Omit both this and callback_url to keep the
stored redirect URIs. Other fields are replaced. Sending an empty list
is an error, not a way to keep the stored list.

scope.description:
Scope replaces the app's current allowlist. Omit to leave the existing
allowlist untouched. Set to an empty string to clear it, making the app
unrestricted.

theme_preference.description:
Deprecated: this value should be retrieved from
`codersdk.UserPreferenceSettings` instead.

path_app_url.description:
PathAppURL is the URL to the base path for path apps. Optional
unless wildcard_hostname is set.
E.g. https://us.example.com

wildcard_hostname.description:
WildcardHostname is the wildcard hostname for subdomain apps.
E.g. *.us.example.com
E.g. *--suffix.au.example.com
Optional. Does not need to be on the same domain as PathAppURL.

created_at.description: CreatedAt is the timestamp when the replica was first seen.

database_latency.description: DatabaseLatency is the latency in microseconds to the database.

hostname.description: Hostname is the hostname of the replica.

id.description: ID is the unique identifier for the replica.

region_id.description: RegionID is the region of the replica.

relay_address.description: RelayAddress is the accessible address to relay DERP connections.

detail.description:
Detail is a debug message that provides further insight into why the
action failed. This information can be technical and a regular golang
err.Error() text.
- "database: too many open connections"
- "stat: too many open files"

message.description:
Message is an actionable message that depicts actions the request took.
These messages should be fully formed sentences with proper punctuation.
Examples:
- "A user has been created."
- "Failed to create a user."

validations.description:
Validations are form field-specific friendly error messages. They will be
shown on a form field in the UI. These can also be used to add additional
context if there is a set of errors in the primary 'Message'.

api_keys.description:
APIKeys controls how long expired API keys are retained before being deleted.
Keys are only deleted if they have been expired for at least this duration.
Defaults to 7 days to preserve existing behavior.

audit_logs.description:
AuditLogs controls how long audit log entries are retained.
Set to 0 to disable (keep indefinitely).

boundary_logs.description:
BoundaryLogs controls how long boundary audit log entries are
retained. Boundary logs record every HTTP request processed by
a Boundary confinement proxy. Set to 0 to disable automatic
deletion (keep indefinitely). Adjust to match your
organization's regulatory requirements.

connection_logs.description:
ConnectionLogs controls how long connection log entries are retained.
Set to 0 to disable (keep indefinitely).

workspace_agent_logs.description:
WorkspaceAgentLogs controls how long workspace agent logs are retained.
Logs are deleted if the agent hasn't connected within this period.
Logs from the latest build are always retained regardless of age.
Defaults to 7 days to preserve existing behavior.

organization_member_permissions.description: OrganizationMemberPermissions are specific for the organization in the field 'OrganizationID' above.

organization_permissions.description: OrganizationPermissions are specific for the organization in the field 'OrganizationID' above.

field.description:
Field is the name of the claim field that specifies what organization roles
a user should be given. If empty, no roles will be synced.

mapping.description: Mapping is a map from OIDC groups to Coder organization roles.

deploymentName.description: DeploymentName is the config-ssh Hostname prefix

sshconfigOptions.description:
SSHConfigOptions are additional options to add to the ssh config file.
This will override defaults.

hostname_prefix.description:
HostnamePrefix is the prefix we append to workspace names for SSH hostnames.
Deprecated: use HostnameSuffix instead.

hostname_suffix.description: HostnameSuffix is the suffix to append to workspace names for SSH hostnames.

display_name.description:
DisplayName is the registry's name for a known app, otherwise the
normalized identifier itself.

family.description: Family is the group this app totals under.

icon.description: Icon is a bundled path under /icon/, empty if the app has none.

apps.description:
Apps holds one entry per reported app name, each carrying the family it
totals under. The fields below duplicate those totals for one release.

jetbrains.description: Deprecated: total Apps by Family instead.

reconnecting_pty.description: Deprecated: total Apps by Family instead.

ssh.description: Deprecated: total Apps by Family instead.

vscode.description: Deprecated: total Apps by Family instead.

default_duration.description: DefaultDuration is only for browser, workspace app and oauth sessions.

disable_expiry_refresh.description:
DisableExpiryRefresh will disable automatically refreshing api
keys when they are used from the api. This means the api key lifetime at
creation is the lifetime of the api key.

refresh_default_duration.description:
RefreshDefaultDuration is the default lifetime for OAuth2 refresh tokens.
This should generally be longer than access token lifetimes to allow
refreshing after access token expiry.

action.description:
Action reports whether a project skill is offered as a one-click
action above project composers. It is always false for personal and
organization skills.

model_invocable.description:
ModelInvocable reports whether agents can discover and load the skill
on their own. Users can still invoke a skill explicitly when it is
false.

action.description:
Action reports whether a project skill is offered as a one-click
action above project composers. It is always false for personal and
organization skills.

model_invocable.description:
ModelInvocable reports whether agents can discover and load the skill
on their own. Users can still invoke a skill explicitly when it is
false.

active_user_count.description: ActiveUserCount is set to -1 when loading.

allow_user_autostart.description:
AllowUserAutostart and AllowUserAutostop are Premium features. Their
values are only used if your license is entitled to use the advanced
template scheduling feature.

allow_workspace_renames.description:
AllowWorkspaceRenames permits users to rename workspaces built from this
template. Renaming can be destructive for templates whose Terraform
references the workspace name.

autostop_requirement.description:
AutostopRequirement and AutostartRequirement are Premium features. Their
values are only used if your license is entitled to use the advanced template
scheduling feature.

disable_module_cache.description:
DisableModuleCache disables the use of cached Terraform modules during
provisioning for this template. It is read-only while
ModuleCacheDisabledByDeployment is true.

failure_ttl_ms.description:
FailureTTLMillis, TimeTilDormantMillis, and TimeTilDormantAutoDeleteMillis are Premium features. Their
values are used if your license is entitled to use the advanced
template scheduling feature.

module_cache_disabled_by_deployment.description:
ModuleCacheDisabledByDeployment reports that the deployment disables the
Terraform module cache for every template. Templates cannot opt back in,
so the effective state is disabled regardless of DisableModuleCache.

require_active_version.description:
RequireActiveVersion mandates that workspaces are built with the active
template version.

time_til_autostop_notify_ms.description:
TimeTilAutostopNotifyMillis is the duration before the workspace's
autostop deadline at which a reminder notification is sent. 0 disables
the notification.

method.description: Method is how the app connected. Method and Slug identify an app.

seconds_is_upper_bound.description:
SecondsIsUpperBound marks overflow usage that includes folded apps.
Their overlap is not stored, so Seconds may overestimate active time.

days_of_week.description:
DaysOfWeek is a list of days of the week in which autostart is allowed
to happen. If no days are specified, autostart is not allowed.

DaysOfWeek is a list of days of the week on which restarts are required.
Restarts happen within the user's quiet hours (in their configured
timezone). If no days are specified, restarts are not required. Weekdays
cannot be specified twice.

Restarts will only happen on weekdays in this list on weeks which line up
with Weeks.

weeks.description:
Weeks is the number of weeks between required restarts. Weeks are synced
across all workspaces (and Coder deployments) using modulo math on a
hardcoded epoch week of January 2nd, 2023 (the first Monday of 2023).
Values of 0 or 1 indicate weekly restarts. Values of 2 indicate
fortnightly restarts, etc.

default.description:
Default reports whether modules attach to this agent when they do not
name one.

agent_name.description: AgentName targets a base coder_agent by name. Empty uses the base default.

session_id.description:
SessionID is the wizard session this request belongs to, as reported to
POST /api/v2/templatebuilder/sessions. It is optional and used only to
attribute a build failure to the session that produced it.

total_member_count.description:
How many members are in this group. Shows the total count,
even if the user is not authorized to read group member details.
May be greater than `len(Group.Members)`.

usage_total_seconds.description:
UsageTotalSeconds counts each user's active minutes once, even when apps
overlap. Summed per-app seconds can exceed this total.

has_ai_seat.description:
HasAISeat intentionally omits omitempty so the API always includes the
field, even when false.

theme_preference.description:
Deprecated: this value should be retrieved from
`codersdk.UserPreferenceSettings` instead.

form_type.description:
FormType has an enum value of empty string, `""`.
Keep the leading comma in the enums struct tag.

service_banner.description: Deprecated: ServiceBanner has been replaced by AnnouncementBanners.

pin_order.description:
PinOrder controls the chat's pinned state and position.
- nil: no change to pin state.
- 0: unpin the chat.
- >0 (chat is unpinned): pin the chat, appending it to
  the end of the pinned list. The specific value is
  ignored; the server assigns the next available position.
- >0 (chat is already pinned): move the chat to the
  requested position, shifting neighbors as needed. The
  value is clamped to [1, pinned_count].

plan_mode.description:
PlanMode switches the chat's persistent plan mode.
nil: no change, ptr to "plan": enable, ptr to "": clear.

project_id.description:
ProjectID moves a root chat, and with it its subagent chats.
- nil: no change.
- uuid.Nil: remove the chat from its project.
- other: move the chat into that project. The chat's owner must own
  the project or have it shared with them, and the project must be
  in the chat's organization.
The server returns 409 while the chat or a subagent chat is not idle.

read.description:
Read moves the owner's read cursor, which drives HasUnread.
- nil: no change.
- true: mark every existing message as read.
- false: clear the cursor so the chat reads as unread again.

The cursor is owner-scoped, so only the chat owner may set this.
Opening a chat's stream marks it read, so marking the chat the
owner is currently viewing as unread does not persist.

title.description:
Title, when set, is stored as the user title even when its text is
unchanged, so a generated title never replaces it afterwards. It is
validated like CreateChatRequest.Title.

workspace_ttl_ms.description:
WorkspaceTTLMillis is the workspace TTL in milliseconds.
Zero means disabled; the template's own autostop setting applies.

current.description: Current indicates whether the server version is the same as the latest.

url.description: URL to download the latest release of Coder.

version.description: Version is the semantic version for the latest release of Coder.

forward_coder_headers.description:
ForwardCoderHeaders, when set, updates whether Coder identity
headers are forwarded on every outgoing MCP request.

oauth2_resource.description:
OAuth2Resource is the RFC 8707 resource indicator. Omit it to keep
the stored value; send "" to clear it.

oauth2_revocation_url.description:
OAuth2RevocationURL is validated in the handler because a
validate tag would reject the pointer to "" that clears it.

signing_secret.description:
SigningSecret replaces the shared signing key. Omit to preserve it;
an empty string clears it. It is never returned.

default_org_member_roles.description:
DefaultOrgMemberRoles, when non-nil, replaces the org's default
member roles.

skills.description:
Skills maps an organization skill ID to whether the skill is enabled
for the member's chats.

action.description: Action is only accepted for project skills.

content.description:
Content must be SKILL.md-format Markdown with YAML frontmatter. The
frontmatter must include name, may include description, and must be
followed by a non-empty body.

group_perms.description:
GroupPerms is a mapping from valid group UUIDs to the template role they
should be granted. To remove a group from the template, use "" as the role
(available as a constant named codersdk.TemplateRoleDeleted)

user_perms.description:
UserPerms is a mapping from valid user UUIDs to the template role they
should be granted. To remove a user from the template, use "" as the role
(available as a constant named codersdk.TemplateRoleDeleted)

activity_bump_ms.description:
ActivityBumpMillis allows optionally specifying the activity bump
duration for all workspaces created from this template. Defaults to 1h
but can be set to 0 to disable activity bumping.

agents_allowed.description:
AgentsAllowed controls whether Coder Agents can create workspaces using
this template. If omitted, the current value is preserved.

allow_workspace_renames.description:
AllowWorkspaceRenames permits users to rename workspaces built from this
template. Renaming can be destructive for templates whose Terraform
references the workspace name.

autostop_requirement.description:
AutostopRequirement and AutostartRequirement can only be set if your license
includes the advanced template scheduling feature. If you attempt to set this
value while unlicensed, it will be ignored.

deprecation_message.description:
DeprecationMessage if set, will mark the template as deprecated and block
any new workspaces from using this template.
If passed an empty string, will remove the deprecated message, making
the template usable for new workspaces again.

disable_everyone_group_access.description:
DisableEveryoneGroupAccess allows optionally disabling the default
behavior of granting the 'everyone' group access to use the template.
If this is set to true, the template will not be available to all users,
and must be explicitly granted to users or groups in the permissions settings
of the template.

disable_module_cache.description:
DisableModuleCache disables the using of cached Terraform modules during
provisioning. It is ignored while the deployment disables the module
cache for all templates. It is recommended not to disable this.

require_active_version.description:
RequireActiveVersion mandates workspaces built using this template
use the active version of the template. This option has no
effect on template admins.

time_til_autostop_notify_ms.description:
TimeTilAutostopNotifyMillis allows optionally specifying the duration
before the autostop deadline at which a reminder notification is sent for
workspaces created from this template. Defaults to 0 (disabled). Omitting
the field keeps the existing value.

update_workspace_dormant_at.description:
UpdateWorkspaceDormantAt updates the dormant_at field of workspaces spawned
from the template. This is useful for preventing dormant workspaces being
immediately deleted when updating the dormant_ttl field to a new, shorter
value.

update_workspace_last_used_at.description:
UpdateWorkspaceLastUsedAt updates the last_used_at field of workspaces
spawned from the template. This is useful for preventing workspaces being
immediately locked when updating the inactivity_ttl field to a new, shorter
value.

use_classic_parameter_flow.description:
UseClassicParameterFlow is a flag that switches the default behavior to use the classic
parameter flow when creating a workspace. This only affects deployments with the experiment
"dynamic-parameters" enabled. This setting will live for a period after the experiment is
made the default.
An "opt-out" is present in case the new feature breaks some existing templates.

theme_dark.description:
ThemeDark is required when ThemeMode is "sync". In "single" mode
an empty value means "preserve the previously persisted slot"
rather than "clear the slot", so partial updates that send only
one slot keep the other intact.

theme_light.description:
ThemeLight is required when ThemeMode is "sync". In "single"
mode an empty value means "preserve the previously persisted
slot" rather than "clear the slot", so partial updates that send
only one slot keep the other intact.

theme_mode.description:
ThemeMode is optional for backward compatibility. When empty,
the server leaves theme_mode, theme_light, and theme_dark
unchanged so older CLI clients do not erase sync-mode settings.
Legacy auto preferences are the exception: they clear theme_mode
so clients can migrate the old sync-with-system setting.

avatar_url.description:
AvatarURL is only applied for users whose login type is password or
none. For other login types the avatar is synced from the identity
provider on login, so a submitted value is ignored.

schedule.description:
Schedule is a cron expression that defines when the user's quiet hours
window is. Schedule must not be empty. For new users, the schedule is set
to 2am in their browser or computer's timezone. The schedule denotes the
beginning of a 4 hour window where the workspace is allowed to
automatically stop or restart due to maintenance or template schedule.

The schedule must be daily with a single time, and should have a timezone
specified via a CRON_TZ prefix (otherwise UTC will be used).

If the schedule is empty, the user will be updated to use the default
schedule.

group_roles.description:
GroupRoles is a mapping from valid group UUIDs to the workspace role they
should be granted. To remove a group from the workspace, use "" as the role
(available as a constant named codersdk.WorkspaceRoleDeleted)

user_roles.description:
UserRoles is a mapping from valid user UUIDs to the workspace role they
should be granted. To remove a user from the workspace, use "" as the role
(available as a constant named codersdk.WorkspaceRoleDeleted)

schedule.description:
Schedule is expected to be of the form `CRON_TZ=<IANA Timezone> <min> <hour> * * <dow>`
Example: `CRON_TZ=US/Central 30 9 * * 1-5` represents 0930 in the timezone US/Central
on weekdays (Mon-Fri). `CRON_TZ` defaults to UTC if not present.

shareable_workspace_owners.description:
ShareableWorkspaceOwners controls whose workspaces can be shared
within the organization.

sharing_disabled.description:
SharingDisabled is deprecated and left for backward compatibility
purposes.
Deprecated: use `ShareableWorkspaceOwners` instead

media_type.description: MediaType is the client-declared content type for display.

name.description: Name is the final basename of the uploaded file.

path.description: Path is the absolute path of the file on the workspace.

size.description: Size is the number of bytes written to the workspace.

workspace_id.description:
WorkspaceID is the workspace whose filesystem received the
bytes. Message parts referencing this upload must carry it.

group_id.description:
GroupID is the group the user's spend is attributed to. The user must
be a member of this group.

has_ai_seat.description:
HasAISeat intentionally omits omitempty so the API always includes the
field, even when false.

theme_preference.description:
Deprecated: this value should be retrieved from
`codersdk.UserPreferenceSettings` instead.

current_spend_micros.description:
CurrentSpendMicros is the user's spend on their effective group over
the current budget period.

effective_budget.description:
EffectiveBudget is the spend limit that applies to the user, whether it
came from a group budget or a user override. Null when no budget
applies, leaving the user's spend unlimited.

effective_group_id.description:
EffectiveGroupID is the group the spend is attributed to, falling back to
the Everyone group when no budget applies. Null only when the user has no
organization membership.

period_end.description:
PeriodEnd is the exclusive upper bound of the current budget
period.

period_start.description:
PeriodStart is the inclusive lower bound of the current budget
period.

theme_preference.description:
ThemePreference is the legacy single-field appearance setting. In
"single" mode it mirrors the active theme. In "sync" mode modern
clients normally mirror the active OS slot, but older clients can
update only this field, so it may diverge from ThemeLight or
ThemeDark until a modern client saves the full appearance state
again.

next.description: Next is the next time that the quiet hours window will start.

time.description:
Time is the time of day that the quiet hours window starts in the given
Timezone each day.

timezone.description: raw format from the cron expression, UTC if unspecified

user_can_set.description:
UserCanSet is true if the user is allowed to set their own quiet hours
schedule. If false, the user cannot set a custom schedule and the default
schedule will always be used.

user_set.description:
UserSet is true if the user has set their own quiet hours schedule. If
false, the user is using the default schedule.

enabled.description:
Enabled controls whether the secret is injected into workspaces.
Disabled secrets remain visible and editable, but are not added
to the agent manifest, so they are not exposed as environment
variables or written to secret files.

file_path_delivery_enabled.description:
FilePathDeliveryEnabled reports whether Coder writes stored file paths
into workspaces. Stored paths are preserved either way.

allow_renames.description:
AllowRenames is the effective rename permission for this workspace,
derived from the template's allow_workspace_renames setting and the
deprecated deployment-wide flag.

deleting_at.description:
DeletingAt indicates the time at which the workspace will be permanently deleted.
A workspace is eligible for deletion if it is dormant (a non-nil dormant_at value)
and a value has been specified for time_til_dormant_autodelete on its template.

dormant_at.description:
DormantAt being non-nil indicates a workspace that is dormant.
A dormant workspace is no longer accessible must be activated.
It is subject to deletion if it breaches
the duration of the time_til_ field on its template.

health.description:
Health shows the health of the workspace and information about
what is causing an unhealthy status.

is_prebuild.description:
IsPrebuild indicates whether the workspace is a prebuilt workspace.
Prebuilt workspaces are owned by the prebuilds system user and have specific behavior,
such as being managed differently from regular workspaces.
Once a prebuilt workspace is claimed by a user, it transitions to a regular workspace,
and IsPrebuild returns false.

owner_name.description: OwnerName is the username of the owner of the workspace.

health.description: Health reports the health of the agent.

latency.description: DERPLatency is mapped by region name (e.g. "New York City", "Seattle").

metadata.description:
Metadata is only populated on the workspaces list endpoint when the
request opts in with the include_agent_metadata search key, and it
only carries the requested keys. The description's script is always
empty here: it can be long, and list consumers want values.

startup_script_behavior.description:
StartupScriptBehavior is a legacy field that is deprecated in favor
of the `coder_script` resource. It's only referenced by old clients.
Deprecated: Remove in the future!

created_at.description: CreatedAt is the time the container was created.

id.description: ID is the unique identifier of the container.

image.description: Image is the name of the container image.

labels.description: Labels is a map of key-value pairs of container labels.

name.description: FriendlyName is the human-readable name of the container.

ports.description: Ports includes ports exposed by the container.

running.description: Running is true if the container is currently running.

status.description:
Status is the current status of the container. This is somewhat
implementation-dependent, but should generally be a human-readable
string.

volumes.description:
Volumes is a map of "things" mounted into the container. Again, this
is somewhat implementation-dependent.

host_ip.description:
HostIP is the IP address of the host interface to which the port is
bound. Note that this can be an IPv4 or IPv6 address.

host_port.description: HostPort is the port number *outside* the container.

network.description: Network is the network protocol used by the port (tcp, udp, etc).

port.description: Port is the port number *inside* the container.

healthy.description: Healthy is true if the agent is healthy.

reason.description: Reason is a human-readable explanation of the agent's health. It is empty if Healthy is true.

containers.description: Containers is a list of containers visible to the workspace agent.

devcontainers.description: Devcontainers is a list of devcontainers visible to the workspace agent.

warnings.description:
Warnings is a list of warnings that may have occurred during the
process of listing containers. This should not include fatal errors.

ports.description:
If there are no ports in the list, nothing should be displayed in the UI.
There must not be a "no ports available" message or anything similar, as
there will always be no ports displayed on platforms where our port
detection logic is unsupported.

age.description:
Age is the number of seconds since the metadata was collected.
It is provided in addition to CollectedAt to protect against clock skew.

dependencies.description:
Dependencies lists the scripts this one waits for, as the
provisioner resolved them. It is omitted when empty.

resource_address.description:
ResourceAddress is the full Terraform address of the coder_script
resource, for example "module.git_clone.coder_script.clone". It is
empty for scripts that are not coder_script resources.

display_name.description: DisplayName is a friendly name for the app.

external.description:
External specifies whether the URL should be opened externally on
the client or not.

healthcheck.description: Healthcheck specifies the configuration for checking app health.

icon.description:
Icon is a relative path or external URL that specifies
an icon to be displayed in the dashboard.

slug.description: Slug is a unique identifier within the agent.

statuses.description: Statuses is a list of statuses for the app.

subdomain.description:
Subdomain denotes whether the app should be accessed via a path on the
`coder server` or via a hostname-based dev URL. If this is set to true
and there is no app wildcard configured on the server, the app will not
be accessible in the UI.

subdomain_name.description: SubdomainName is the application domain exposed on the `coder server`.

tooltip.description:
Tooltip is an optional markdown supported field that is displayed
when hovering over workspace apps in the UI.

url.description:
URL is the address being proxied to inside the workspace.
If external is specified, this will be opened on the client.

icon.description:
Deprecated: This field is unused and will be removed in a future version.
Icon is an external URL to an icon that will be rendered in the UI.

needs_user_attention.description:
Deprecated: This field is unused and will be removed in a future version.
NeedsUserAttention specifies whether the status needs user attention.

uri.description:
URI is the URI of the resource that the status is for.
e.g. https://github.com/org/repo/pull/123
e.g. file:///path/to/file

workspace_owner_name.description: WorkspaceOwnerName is the username of the owner of the workspace.

id.description:
ID identifies this click so a later step of the funnel can be
attributed to it.

agent_script_timings.description:
TODO: Consolidate agent-related timing metrics into a single struct when
updating the API version

total_member_count.description:
How many members are in this group. Shows the total count,
even if the user is not authorized to read group member details.
May be greater than `len(Group.Members)`.

failing_agents.description: FailingAgents lists the IDs of the agents that are failing, if any.

healthy.description: Healthy is true if the workspace is healthy.

path_app_url.description:
PathAppURL is the URL to the base path for path apps. Optional
unless wildcard_hostname is set.
E.g. https://us.example.com

status.description:
Status is the latest status check of the proxy. This will be empty for deleted
proxies. This value can be used to determine if a workspace proxy is healthy
and ready to use.

wildcard_hostname.description:
WildcardHostname is the wildcard hostname for subdomain apps.
E.g. *.us.example.com
E.g. *--suffix.au.example.com
Optional. Does not need to be on the same domain as PathAppURL.

report.description: Report provides more information about the health of the workspace proxy.

cleared_at.description:
ClearedAt is set once a later build superseded the secret and its
value was dropped. Cleared secrets are not delivered and replace
nothing.

enabled.description:
Enabled controls whether the secret is injected into workspaces.
Disabled secrets remain visible and editable, but are not added
to the agent manifest, so they are not exposed as environment
variables or written to secret files.

env_replaces.description:
EnvReplaces is the ID of the workspace owner's user secret that this
secret displaces on env_name.

ephemeral.description:
Ephemeral secrets are delivered to their build only and not copied to
the next one.

file_replaces.description:
FileReplaces is the ID of the workspace owner's user secret that this
secret displaces on file_path.

env_name.description:
EnvName is the environment variable to inject the secret as. Empty
means no env injection. Required when file_path is empty and value is
set.

ephemeral.description:
Ephemeral secrets are delivered to this build only and are not
carried forward to the next build.

file_path.description:
FilePath is the path to write the secret to inside the workspace.
Empty means no file is written. Deployments may disable file path
delivery.

value.description:
Value is the plaintext secret. A null value removes the secret. An
empty string sets an empty secret.

shareable_workspace_owners.description:
ShareableWorkspaceOwners controls whose workspaces can be shared
within the organization.

sharing_disabled.description:
SharingDisabled is deprecated and left for backward compatibility
purposes.
Deprecated: use `ShareableWorkspaceOwners` instead

sharing_globally_disabled.description:
SharingGloballyDisabled is true if sharing has been disabled for this
organization because of a deployment-wide setting.

key.description: Key is the public key of the client which sent/received these bytes.

tokenBucketBytesBurst.description:
TokenBucketBytesBurst is how many bytes the server will
allow to burst, temporarily violating
TokenBucketBytesPerSecond.

Zero means unspecified. There might be a limit, but the
client need not try to respect it.

tokenBucketBytesPerSecond.description:
TokenBucketBytesPerSecond is how many bytes per second the
server says it will accept, including all framing bytes.

Zero means unspecified. There might be a limit, but the
client need not try to respect it.

active.description: Active is a ptr to prevent the empty value from being interpreted as false.

captivePortal.description:
CaptivePortal is set when we think there's a captive portal that is
intercepting HTTP traffic.

ipv4CanSend.description: an IPv4 packet was able to be sent

ipv6.description: an IPv6 STUN round trip completed

ipv6CanSend.description: an IPv6 packet was able to be sent

mappingVariesByDestIP.description:
MappingVariesByDestIP is whether STUN results depend which
STUN server you're talking to (on IPv4).

pcp.description:
PCP is whether PCP appears present on the LAN.
Empty means not checked.

pmp.description:
PMP is whether NAT-PMP appears present on the LAN.
Empty means not checked.

udp.description: a UDP STUN round trip completed

upnP.description:
UPnP is whether UPnP appears present on the LAN.
Empty means not checked.

annotations.description:
Annotations enable extensions to serpent higher up in the stack. It's useful for
help formatting and documentation generation.

default.description:
Default is parsed into Value if set.
Must be `""` if `DefaultFn` != nil

env.description:
Env is the environment variable used to configure this option. If unset,
environment configuring is disabled.

flag.description:
Flag is the long name of the flag used to configure this option. If unset,
flag configuring is disabled.

flag_shorthand.description:
FlagShorthand is the one-character shorthand for the flag. If unset, no
shorthand is used.

group.description:
Group is a group hierarchy that helps organize this option in help, configs
and other documentation.

required.description:
Required means this value must be set by some means. It requires
`ValueSource != ValueSourceNone`
If `Default` is set, then `Required` is ignored.

use_instead.description:
UseInstead is a list of options that should be used instead of this one.
The field is used to generate a deprecation warning.

value.description: Value includes the types listed in values.go.

yaml.description:
YAML is the YAML key used to configure this option. If unset, YAML
configuring is disabled.

forceQuery.description:
ForceQuery indicates whether the original URL contained a query ('?') character.
When set, the String method will include a trailing '?', even when RawQuery is empty.

omitHost.description:
OmitHost indicates the URL has an empty host (authority).
When set, the String method will not include the host when it is empty.

path.description: path (relative paths may omit leading slash)

rawFragment.description:
RawFragment is an optional field containing an encoded fragment hint.
See the EscapedFragment method for more details.

In general, code should call EscapedFragment instead of reading RawFragment.

rawPath.description:
RawPath is an optional field containing an encoded path hint.
See the EscapedPath method for more details.

In general, code should call EscapedPath instead of reading RawPath.

rawQuery.description:
RawQuery contains the encoded query values, without the initial '?'.
Use URL.Query to decode the query.

regionScore.description:
RegionScore scales latencies of DERP regions by a given scaling
factor when determining which region to use as the home
("preferred") DERP. Scores in the range (0, 1) will cause this
region to be proportionally more preferred, and scores in the range
(1, ∞) will penalize a region.

If a region is not present in this map, it is treated as having a
score of 1.0.

Scores should not be 0 or negative; such scores will be ignored.

A nil map means no change from the previous value (if any); an empty
non-nil map can be sent to reset all scores back to 1.0.

homeParams.description:
HomeParams, if non-nil, is a change in home parameters.

The rest of the DEPRMap fields, if zero, means unchanged.

omitDefaultRegions.description:
OmitDefaultRegions specifies to not use Tailscale's DERP servers, and only use those
specified in this DERPMap. If there are none set outside of the defaults, this is a noop.

This field is only meaningful if the Regions map is non-nil (indicating a change).

regions.description:
Regions is the set of geographic regions running DERP node(s).

It's keyed by the DERPRegion.RegionID.

The numbers are not necessarily contiguous.

canPort80.description:
CanPort80 specifies whether this DERP node is accessible over HTTP
on port 80 specifically. This is used for captive portal checks.

certName.description:
CertName optionally specifies the expected TLS cert common
name. If empty, HostName is used. If CertName is non-empty,
HostName is only used for the TCP dial (if IPv4/IPv6 are
not present) + TLS ClientHello.

derpport.description:
DERPPort optionally provides an alternate TLS port number
for the DERP HTTPS server.

If zero, 443 is used.

forceHTTP.description:
ForceHTTP is used by unit tests to force HTTP.
It should not be set by users.

hostName.description:
HostName is the DERP node's hostname.

It is required but need not be unique; multiple nodes may
have the same HostName but vary in configuration otherwise.

insecureForTests.description:
InsecureForTests is used by unit tests to disable TLS verification.
It should not be set by users.

ipv4.description:
IPv4 optionally forces an IPv4 address to use, instead of using DNS.
If empty, A record(s) from DNS lookups of HostName are used.
If the string is not an IPv4 address, IPv4 is not used; the
conventional string to disable IPv4 (and not use DNS) is
"none".

ipv6.description:
IPv6 optionally forces an IPv6 address to use, instead of using DNS.
If empty, AAAA record(s) from DNS lookups of HostName are used.
If the string is not an IPv6 address, IPv6 is not used; the
conventional string to disable IPv6 (and not use DNS) is
"none".

name.description:
Name is a unique node name (across all regions).
It is not a host name.
It's typically of the form "1b", "2a", "3b", etc. (region
ID + suffix within that region)

regionID.description:
RegionID is the RegionID of the DERPRegion that this node
is running in.

stunonly.description:
STUNOnly marks a node as only a STUN server and not a DERP
server.

stunport.description:
Port optionally specifies a STUN port to use.
Zero means 3478.
To disable STUN on this node, use -1.

stuntestIP.description:
STUNTestIP is used in tests to override the STUN server's IP.
If empty, it's assumed to be the same as the DERP server.

avoid.description:
Avoid is whether the client should avoid picking this as its home
region. The region should only be used if a peer is there.
Clients already using this region as their home should migrate
away to a new region without Avoid set.

embeddedRelay.description:
EmbeddedRelay is true when the region is bundled with the Coder
control plane.

nodes.description:
Nodes are the DERP nodes running in this region, in
priority order for the current client. Client TLS
connections should ideally only go to the first entry
(falling back to the second if necessary). STUN packets
should go to the first 1 or 2.

If nodes within a region route packets amongst themselves,
but not to other regions. That said, each user/domain
should get a the same preferred node order, so if all nodes
for a user/network pick the first one (as they should, when
things are healthy), the inter-cluster routing is minimal
to zero.

regionCode.description:
RegionCode is a short name for the region. It's usually a popular
city or airport code in the region: "nyc", "sf", "sin",
"fra", etc.

regionID.description:
RegionID is a unique integer for a geographic region.

It corresponds to the legacy derpN.tailscale.com hostnames
used by older clients. (Older clients will continue to resolve
derpN.tailscale.com when contacting peers, rather than use
the server-provided DERPMap)

RegionIDs must be non-zero, positive, and guaranteed to fit
in a JavaScript number.

RegionIDs in range 900-999 are reserved for end users to run their
own DERP nodes.

regionName.description:
RegionName is a long English name for the region: "New York City",
"San Francisco", "Singapore", "Frankfurt", etc.

app_hostname.description:
AppHostname is the optional hostname for subdomain apps on the external
proxy. It must start with an asterisk.

app_path.description: AppPath is the path of the user underneath the app base path.

app_query.description: AppQuery is the query parameters the user provided in the app request.

session_token.description: SessionToken is the session token provided by the user.

agent_name_or_id.description: AgentNameOrID is not required if the workspace has only one agent.

app_prefix.description:
Prefix is the prefix of the subdomain app URL. Prefix should have a
trailing "---" if set.

base_path.description:
BasePath of the app. For path apps, this is the path prefix in the router
for this particular app. For subdomain apps, this should be "/". This is
used for setting the cookie path.

username_or_id.description:
For the following fields, if the AccessMethod is AccessMethodTerminal,
then only AgentNameOrID may be set and it must be a UUID. The other
fields must be left blank.

session_ended_at.description: Updated periodically while app is in use active and when the last connection is closed.

ReplicaID is a unique identifier for the replica of the proxy that is
deregistering. It should be generated by the client on startup and
should've already been passed to the register endpoint.

signed_token_str.description: SignedTokenStr should be set as a cookie on the response.

access_url.description: AccessURL that hits the workspace proxy api.

derp_enabled.description:
DerpEnabled indicates whether the proxy should be included in the DERP
map or not.

derp_only.description:
DerpOnly indicates whether the proxy should only be included in the DERP
map and should not be used for serving apps.

hostname.description:
ReplicaHostname is the OS hostname of the machine that the proxy is running
on.  This is only used for tracking purposes in the replicas table.

replica_error.description:
ReplicaError is the error that the replica encountered when trying to
dial it's peers. This is stored in the replicas table for debugging
purposes but does not affect the proxy's ability to register.

This value is only stored on subsequent requests to the register
endpoint, not the first request.

ReplicaID is a unique identifier for the replica of the proxy that is
registering. It should be generated by the client on startup and
persisted (in memory only) until the process is restarted.

ReplicaRelayAddress is the DERP address of the replica that other
replicas may use to connect internally for DERP meshing.

wildcard_hostname.description: WildcardHostname that the workspace proxy api is serving for subdomain apps.

sibling_replicas.description:
SiblingReplicas is a list of all other replicas of the proxy that have
not timed out.
